mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an easing monetary policy shift that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% in the prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% over the prior month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) over the prior month signal a weakening housing market that reduces consumer spending and economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where both RSAFS and HOUST decline by at least 1.0% in the prior month, or the interaction effect's Rank IC is negative in any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100 and falling for three consecutive months), manufacturing output contraction signals reduced corporate capacity utilization and earnings pressure, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: industrial production contraction (INDPRO < 100 and declining for 3 months)
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the INDPRO contraction regime, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior month reflects robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods with PAYEMS growth exceeding 100k, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in CPI inflation above 2.5% signals rising price pressures that may trigger premature monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL y/y growth exceeds 2.5%, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a 'soft landing' scenario where the economy avoids recession while the Fed tightens, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the interaction effect's Rank IC is negative in any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 annualized growth rate below 1.5%), the economy is entering a slowdown phase that reduces corporate profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where GDPC1 annualized growth rate is below 1.5%, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.
